subject.title: [Bug]: In msteams channel messages, OpenClaw can't access inbound attachments

question: Should the Microsoft Teams plugin always attempt Graph message fetches for non-personal text/html stubs when direct media extraction finds no media, or should that behavior be behind a channel configuration flag?
rationale: The bug is real and documented behavior expects Graph-backed channel files, but the repair changes the steady-state Graph lookup policy for channel/group messages and may affect high-volume deployments.

options.title: Land the plugin fallback without new config
options.body: Accept the linked PR shape because it fixes documented Graph-backed media behavior inside the Teams plugin and avoids adding another config surface.

options.title: Gate Graph fallback with an explicit option
options.body: Require a config-gated variant if maintainers decide the extra Graph message GET per markerless text/html group/channel message is too costly as default behavior.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Leave channel/group file attachments broken for markerless Bot Framework payloads until a lower-cost detection signal is available.

recommendation.title: Land the plugin fallback without new config
recommendation.body: Accept the linked PR shape because it fixes documented Graph-backed media behavior inside the Teams plugin and avoids adding another config surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is a plugin-boundary and default-policy decision, and this history points to steipete as the Microsoft Teams plugin migration/boundary contributor.
